alice: Quick TL;DR — I ran a topology sweep for llama-3-13b-q4 across PCIe vs SXM nodes in us-west-2 and us-east-1. Short summary: NVLink + explicit NUMA pinning consistently reduces p99 by ~25% and increases throughput ~1.6x for 2x GPU infer (batch=1). On several PCIe nodes the runtime falls back to a generic attention kernel which adds ~10–15% latency.
raj: Nice. Can you paste the exact commands and the hw mapping you used? Want to reproduce.
alice: Sure — here's the run invocation and the pinning we used:
```bash
# node type: sxm-a100-2x vs pcie-a100-2x (same cores)
export MODEL=llama-3-13b-q4
export BATCH=1
# pin python + worker threads to socket 0, allow GPUs 0,1
numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 \
  python -m redwood.runtime.infer \
    --model $MODEL --devices 0,1 --batch $BATCH \
    --use-kv-cache --quant q4_0 \
    --trace /tmp/perf_trace.json
```
On SXM we left CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 and didn't set numactl for a baseline run.
megan: Which kernels did you see selected? fused-attn, cutlass, cuBLAS, or generic kernels?
alice: From the perf traces:
perf-bot: kernel-selection: [sxm-node] fused_attention_fp16_fast x 72%, cutlass_gemm x 18%, cudnn_conv_like x 10%
perf-bot: kernel-selection: [pcie-node] generic_attention x 58%, cutlass_gemm x 28%, cudnn_conv_like x 14%
The big delta is fused_attention_fp16_fast present on SXM (due to NVLink-friendly tensor layout) and mostly missing on PCIe which ended up with generic_attention for many layers.
eva: Any eval/quality regressions from the q4 quantization after these runtime changes?
alice: No meaningful quality regressions on our eval set (common prompts + safety set). Token-level BLEU-ish delta ~ -0.3% on a 5k example eval. So perf differences are not model quality related.
simon: What about cache effects / KV-share across GPUs? Did you test warm vs cold cache?
alice: Yes. Warm cache with repeated prompt patterns shows throughput win becomes larger (SXM ~1.8x) since NVLink makes KV sharing cheap. Cold-cache p99 shows the biggest gap on PCIe — cache populate copies over PCIe cost a lot.
derek: Can you drop a tiny chart or numbers for capacity guidance? e.g., tokens/sec and p99 for the 2-GPU config.
alice: mini table (median latency in ms, p99 in ms, tokens/s total):
SXM (us-west-2): median 18ms, p99 45ms, tokens/s 1650
PCIE (us-west-2): median 26ms, p99 60ms, tokens/s 980
SXM (us-east-1): median 20ms, p99 48ms, tokens/s 1580
PCIE (us-east-1): median 28ms, p99 67ms, tokens/s 920
These are single-run averages (batch=1, 2x GPUs, mixed-fp16 + q4 inference). We also saw higher variance on PCIe for high concurrency.
megan: Looks like kernel selection + NVLink is the main driver, plus NUMA placement. We should consider exposing a runtime knob to prefer fused kernels and pin-to-socket heuristics when NVLink is present.
raj: Agree. Also need to check autoscaler interactions — if we scale up pods without preserving NUMA/GPU affinity we could lose these wins.
simon: For capacity sizing, would you recommend different reserve factors for PCIe vs SXM?
alice: Yes — ballpark: for the same SLO target use ~1.7x more PCIe capacity (or increase target latency SLO by ~1.5x). For bursty traffic add another 10–20% headroom on PCIe due to higher variance.
megan: Action items?
- raj -> open an infra issue to add "topology-aware" node label and a runtime flag to prefer fused kernels when NVLink detected
- alice -> upload full perf traces + perf-bot artifacts (raw traces, flamegraphs)
- eva -> run the same sweep with 4x GPU config and share numbers (to check cross-gpu scaling)
raj: I'll create the issue and link the traces. thanks all.
